newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto considers splitting its operations.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto considers splitting its operations.

text.p: Monsanto Co. said Thursday it was considering several alternatives for its future, including splitting into two corporations -- one a life sciences company and the other a chemical concern.
"In recent years, the strategies and needs of the chemical and life sciences businesses have become quite different," Chairman Robert Shapiro said in a statement.
"It's in the best interest of our people, our customers and our shareowners that we take appropriate steps to allow all of our businesses to reach their maximum potential."
The company's stock gained $1 to $41.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in early trading.
Monsanto, based in St. Louis, manufactures a variety of chemicals, agriculture products, plastics and pharmaceuticals.
While chemicals accounted for more than 40 percent of the company's $8.96 billion in sales last year, that segment continues to experience declining revenues and margins.

A spokeswoman said options under study included the possible merger of the chemical businesses into companies outside of Monsanto. Or Monsanto could opt to keep the chemical businesses and restructure them, she said.
Shapiro said the company would move as quickly as it could to make a decision, "... but we'll take the time needed to make the right decisions."
The chemical businesses include nylon fibers, speciality chemicals and Saflex, a plastic interlayer sold to glass manufacturers.
